Hi Jared — thanks again for making time today. Quick recap from our side so we have alignment on scope and next steps. I’ve attached a short one‑pager and an SDK checklist (stub) that Ben will flesh out with technical items.

Key pain we heard
- Latency-sensitive triage pipeline: your L1 triage UI needs sub‑250ms response for streaming suggestions to feel real-time.
- Deterministic structured outputs: downstream systems require consistent JSON schema from assistant actions for routing and automation.
- Vector search + rerank for triage relevance: current keyword match yields noisy results; you want dense embeddings + a lightweight reranker to surface top suggestions.

Goals we agreed on
1) Proof-of-concept (2–4 weeks): streaming suggestions in the triage UI + output schema enforcement for 1 flow.
2) Evaluate embeddings + reranker for recall/precision improvements over current TF-IDF baseline.
3) Identify latency and cost tradeoffs for deployment (hosted vs. dedicated).

Technical notes / constraints you mentioned
- Preferred language: TypeScript backend.
- On‑prem data isolation required for certain patient data (will need Private deployment conversation).
- Your sequences average 150 tokens for prompts, with occasional 1k token context when triage history is included.

Recommended initial approach
- Use Redwood streaming SDK to stream token deltas into the UI and expose a function-calling layer for structured decisions (JSON schema v1 attached).
- Run embeddings for candidate retrieval (small, 1536-d) and a light reranker model (distil-style) colocated with the vector store to keep latency down.
- For determinism, we’ll apply structured output schemas + mild temperature and log-prob thresholds; for critical routes fallback to a compact non-streaming path.

Next steps (owners & dates)
- Ben: SDK integration checklist and gap items (by Mon 9/14).
- Monica: sample JSON schema for function calls and example responses (by Tue 9/15).
- Aperture: confirm a dev host (internal cloud) we can use for the POC and any required security contacts (procurement/SecOps) (by Mon 9/14).

Attachments: aperture-integration-summary-20260912.pdf (one-pager), sdk-integration-checklist.xlsx (stub)

Thanks — I’ll set a short sync for early next week once Ben posts the checklist.

Jared — quick technical follow-up and an initial checklist attached. Highlights / clarifications:
- Streaming: Redwood's streaming SDK supports chunked token delivery and a token-level progress callback in our TypeScript client. Expect ~15–25ms extra latency per token for standard 8-bit quantized runs on a dedicated GPU; end-to-end UI latency will also depend on your frontend batching strategy.
- Function calling / structured output: we suggest a schema-driven validator (server-side) that attempts 2 quick fixes if output parsing fails (1. whitespace/bracket normalization; 2. simple key insertion from heuristics). If still invalid, mark for manual triage.
- Embeddings & rerank: start with 1536-d dense vectors (we can provide embeddings server or run locally). Reranker should run as a small forward pass (under 8ms p95 when colocated).
- Model picks: for POC use rw-infer-small (cost friendly) for embeddings + rw-fluent-compact for rerank; we’ll switch models for accuracy testing.

What I attached: sdk-integration-checklist.xlsx (detailed integration tasks), small-demo-config.json.sample (stub), latency-measure-template.csv (to capture p50/p95).

Open items for Aperture
- Do you have an internal vector store (we can plug into Pinecone/FAISS) or should we provide one in the demo environment?
- Confirm whether sample data can be used in dev host (anonymized triage records).

I’ll prep a quick TypeScript integration snippet showing streaming + function call handler by EOD Mon.
